content: 1. Bellinger DC authored a study in 2004, published in Pediatrics, volume 113, issue 4, pages 1016–1022. 2. The International Atomic Energy Association and the World Health Organization published a report in Vienna in 2015 on protecting the public from indoor exposure to radon and other natural radiation sources. 3. Clero E, Marie CL, Challeton-De Vathaire C, Laurier D, and Rannou A conducted an evaluation of radon-induced health risks for individuals living in homes built on uranium ore residues, published in Revue d’Epidemiologie et de Sante Publique in 2016. 4. Lim SS, Vos T, Flaxman AD, Danaei G, Shibuya K, Adair-Rohani H, and colleagues performed a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2010, assessing the burden of disease and injury attributable to 67 risk factors across 21 regions from 1990 to 2010. This was published in The Lancet in 2012, volume 380, issue 9589, pages 2224–2260. 5. Braubach M, Jacobs DE, and Ormandy D authored a report on the environmental burden of disease associated with inadequate housing, published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2011. 6. Pfadenhauer LM, Gerhardus A, Mozygemba K, Lysdahl KB, Booth A, Hofmann B, and colleagues developed the Context and Implementation of Complex Interventions (CICI) framework to address complexity in context and implementation. This was published in Implementation Science in 2017, volume 12, article 21. 7. Figueras J and McKee M edited a book titled Health systems, health, wealth, and societal well-being: assessing the case for investing in health systems, published by Open University Press in Maidenhead, United Kingdom, in 2012. 8. Jackson G, Thornley S, Woolston J, Papa D, Bernacchi A, and Moore T reported on reduced acute hospitalizations associated with the Healthy Housing Programme in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health in 2011, volume 65, issue 7, pages 588–593. 9. Takaro TK, Krieger J, Song L, Sharify D, and Beaudet N studied the impact of asthma-friendly home construction on clinical outcomes and trigger exposure, published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2011, volume 101, issue 1, pages 55–62. 10. Galiani S, Gertler PJ, Undurraga R, Cooper R, Martínez S, and Ross A examined the effects of upgrading housing infrastructure in Latin American slums, published in the Journal of Urban Economics in 2017, volume 98, pages 187–213. 11. Sundell J, Levin H, Nazaroff WW, Cain WS, Fisk WJ, Grimsrud DT, and colleagues conducted a multidisciplinary review of scientific literature on ventilation rates and health, published in Indoor Air in 2011, volume 21, issue 3, pages 191–204. 12. Beck AF, Huang B, Chundur R, and Kahn RS found an association between housing code violation density and emergency department and hospital use by children with asthma, published in Health Affairs in 2014, volume 33, issue 11, pages 1993–2002. 13. Krieger J and Jacobs D contributed a chapter on healthy housing in the book Making healthy places: designing and building for health, well-being, and sustainability, edited by Dannenberg AL, Frumkin H, and Jackson RJ, and published by Island Press in Washington, DC, in 2011. 14. Rozendaal JA authored a guide on vector control methods for individuals and communities, published by the World Health Organization in Geneva in 1997. 15. Stranden E, Kolstad AK, and Lind B studied the influence of moisture and temperature on radon exhalation, published in Radiation Protection Dosimetry in 1984, volume 7, issues 1–4, pages 55–58. 16. Brown MJ analyzed the costs and benefits of enforcing housing policies to prevent childhood lead poisoning, published in Medical Decision Making in 2002, volume 22, issue 6, pages 482–492. 17. Dixon SL, Jacobs DE, Wilson JW, Akoto JY, Nevin R, and Scott Clark C evaluated the long-term effects of window replacement on residential lead paint hazard control, published in Environmental Research in 2012, volume 113, pages 14–20. 18. Gould E provided conservative estimates of the social and economic benefits of lead hazard control in preventing childhood lead poisoning, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2009, volume 117, issue 7, pages 1162–1167. 19. Nevin R, Jacobs DE, Berg M, and Cohen J assessed the monetary benefits of preventing childhood lead poisoning through lead-safe window replacement, published in Environmental Research in 2008, volume 106, issue 3, pages 410–419. 20. Pichery C, Bellanger M, Zmirou-Navier D, Glorennec P, Hartemann P, and Grandjean P estimated the benefits and conducted a partial cost-benefit analysis of lead hazard control in France, published in Environmental Health in 2011, volume 10, article 44. 21. Chapman R, Howden-Chapman P, Viggers H, O’Dea D, and Kennedy M performed a cost-benefit analysis of retrofitting houses with insulation as part of a randomized community trial, published in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health in 2009, volume 63, issue 4, pages 271–277. 22. Levy JI, Nishioka Y, and Spengler JD evaluated the public health benefits of insulation retrofits in existing housing in the United States, published in Environmental Health in 2003, volume 2, article 4. 23. Hutton G, Haller L, and Bartram J conducted a global cost-benefit analysis of water supply and sanitation interventions, published in the Journal of Water Health in 2007, volume 5, issue 4, pages 481–502. 24. Aiga H and Umenai T studied the impact of water supply improvement on household economy in a squatter area of Manila, published in Social Science & Medicine in 2002, volume 55, issue 4, pages 627–641. 25. Cattaneo MD, Galiani S, Gertler PJ, Martinez S, and Titiunik R explored the relationship between housing, health, and happiness in a policy research working paper published by the World Bank in Washington, DC, in 2007. 26. Nurmagambetov TA, Barnett SB, Jacob V, Chattopadhyay SK, Hopkins DP, Crocker DD, and colleagues conducted a systematic review on the economic value of home-based, multi-trigger, multicomponent interventions for reducing asthma morbidity, published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2011, volume 41, supplement 1, pages S33–S47. 27. Campbell JD, Brooks M, Hosokawa P, Robinson J, Song L, and Krieger J evaluated the effects of community health worker home visits on asthma outcomes and costs for Medicaid-enrolled children, published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2015, volume 105, issue 11, pages 2366–2372. 28. Woods ER, Bhaumik U, Sommer SJ, Ziniel SI, Kessler AJ, Chan E, and colleagues assessed the Community Asthma Initiative, a quality improvement program for comprehensive asthma care, published in Pediatrics in 2012, volume 129, issue 3, pages 465–472. 29. Bhaumik U, Norris K, Charron G, Walker SP, Sommer SJ, Chan E, and colleagues conducted a cost analysis of a community-based case management intervention program for pediatric asthma, published in the Journal of Asthma in 2013, volume 50, issue 3, pages 310–317. 30. Eurofound published a report on the costs and consequences of inadequate housing in Europe, released by the Publications Office of the European Union in Luxembourg in 2016. 31. Waters SF, Boyce WT, Eskenazi B, and Alkon A studied the impact of maternal depression and overcrowded housing on the relationship between autonomic nervous system reactivity and externalizing behavior problems in vulnerable Latino children, published in Psychophysiology in 2016, volume 53, issue 1, pages 97–104. 32. Perry S, de la Luz Sanchez M, Hurst PK, and Parsonnet J investigated household transmission of gastroenteritis, published in Emerging Infectious Diseases in 2005, volume 11, pages 1093–1096. 33. Asamoah B, Kjellstrom T, and Östergren PO examined the association between ambient heat exposure levels and miscarriage or stillbirths in hot regions, using data from the Ghana Maternal Health Survey 2007, published in the International Journal of Biometeorology in 2018, volume 62, pages 319–330.
